purpose: Provide an AI-readable example for generating a static mesh and PBR textures that can be integrated into an existing SC2 Zergling rig without inventing a new skeleton or animation contract.

rigContract.attachmentAndCollisionPolicy: Preserve template attachment points and hit-test data; do not generate replacement groups for these entries.

weightPolicy.requiredBeforeExport: Every mesh vertex has at least one positive deform-group weight.
weightPolicy.maximumInfluences: Use the local authoring convention and inspect joints, forelegs, rear legs, feet, and tail manually.

actionContract.samplingPolicy: Review start, middle, and end frames for every required action after each mesh or weight change.
actionContract.acceptance: No visible mesh flight, joint separation, tail collapse, or unacceptable stretching in the three required actions.
actionContract.priority: Reuse template actions first; do not redesign Animation Groups or M3A data during mesh generation.

output.mesh: One static GLB with one mesh and preserved UVs; no final SC2 skeleton or animation required.
output.provenance: Record generator, source prompt or image set, version, triangle count, texture sizes, and output hashes.

doNotGenerate: Replacement attachment points or hit-test volumes

geometryGuidance.axisAndOrigin: Match the template after the declared GLB import axis correction and place the mesh at Ref_Origin.
geometryGuidance.proportions: Match body, pelvis, head, four limb chains, feet, and tail landmarks before weight transfer.
geometryGuidance.topology: Keep enough edge flow around joints and tail segments for local Weight Paint; avoid a single rigid shell across moving limbs.

selectedExample.reason: All vertices receive transferred template deform weights and the canonical actions drive the mesh, but the body and tail alignment still require manual W4 visual correction.

negativeExamples.reason: The whole mesh follows one bone and cannot preserve local limb or tail motion.
Unreviewed automatic methods can leave vertices unweighted or create long-bar deformation; numeric motion alone is not anatomical validation.

negativeExamples.mode: rest-bone-retarget, affine group fit, landmark surface fit, segment weighting
negativeExamples.reason: Existing offline probes produced bone detachment, long-bar stretching, local collapse, or worse rigid-looking sections.

experimentalCouplingExample.lesson: Use the x-ray certificates and complete playback reel to verify that the Armature modifier, weights, and reused actions actually move the AI surface. Do not mistake visible skeleton-to-mesh coupling for anatomical W4 clearance: the v41 fitted-segment experiment remains non-production until the generated mesh matches the template body, limb anchors, tail path, and action semantics.

qualityGates: Static mesh and PBR maps load without changing the template source asset.
Mesh aligns to template axis, origin, and major body/limb/tail landmarks.
Every vertex is weighted to canonical deform groups and non-skin groups remain excluded.
Stand, Walk, and Attack pass start-middle-end visual review.
Candidate M3 exports and re-imports with the expected rig, mesh, UV, and action structure.
SC2 Previewer, Actor, and in-game behavior are a separate future runtime gate.
scopeBoundary: This reference package contains offline Blender/M3Studio evidence only. It does not prove SC2 Previewer, Actor, map, mod, or in-game runtime compatibility.
